visual_action: A montage of clips of the singer Ariana Grande, from what appear to be music videos and performances, plays. Throughout the video, a static image of a tweet from the account 'Pop Base' is overlaid in the center of the screen. The tweet claims that Grande has condemned the White House for using one ofher songs in a TikTok about ICE.

cast.name: Ariana Grande
cast.evidence: She is shown in every clip of the video and is the subject of the on-screen tweet.

cast.name: The White House
cast.evidence: The on-screen tweet states that Ariana Grande 'slams the White House'.

cast.name: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE)
cast.evidence: The on-screen tweet mentions 'a TikTok of ICE agents arresting people'.

cast.name: Pop Base
cast.evidence: The tweet shown on screen is from the account 'Pop Base @PopBase'.

on_screen_text.text:
Pop Base @PopBase

Ariana Grande slams the White House for using her song 'bye' in a TikTok of ICE agents arresting people:

"Please do not ever use my music in relation to this barbaric, inhumane, heinous nonsense"

spoken_summary: There is no spoken dialogue in the video. The audio consists of the lyrics of the song 'Everyday' by Ariana Grande.
audio_music: A continuous, upbeat pop/R&B track, identified as Ariana Grande's song 'Everyday', plays throughout the entire video. The music creates the feel of a fan-edit celebrating the artist.
editing_pacing: The video is a fast-paced montage with quick cuts between various clips of Ariana Grande every one to two seconds.
central_claim: Ariana Grande has condemned the White House and ICE for using her music, calling their actions 'barbaric, inhumane, heinous nonsense'.
intended_effect: To leverage Ariana Grande's celebrity and her strong condemnation to foster negative sentiment towards the White House and its immigration policies as enforced by ICE.
uncertainty_flags: The authenticity of the tweet from Pop Base cannot be verified from the video alone.
The video does not show the alleged White House TikTok that is the subject of the tweet's claim.
The on-screen tweet claims the controversy is over the song 'bye', but the song playing in this video is 'Everyday' by Ariana Grande.
